Delegate

/DEL-uh-gayt/ · verb

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Delegate means to hand over a task or responsibility to someone else, usually someone working under your direction.

Delegate means to hand over a task or responsibility to someone else. Swamped with paperwork, the restaurant manager chose to delegate the weekly supply orders to her assistant, and she soon learned to delegate the staff schedule as well.

Worked Example

Instead of painting every poster herself, the student council president decided to delegate the artwork to the decorations committee.

The president hands the poster job over to people she directs, keeping her own time free for other duties. Passing responsibility downward like this is the heart of delegating.

How Delegate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

assign

assign: to give out as a task

entrust

entrust: to hand over with confidence

transfer

transfer: to move a duty to another person

Antonyms

retain

retain: to keep for oneself

hoard

hoard: to refuse to share or hand over

How Strong Is It? — assign → delegate → relinquish

assign vs. delegate

assign vs. delegate: To assign a task is just to hand it out — a teacher assigns homework without giving up any duties of her own.

relinquish vs. delegate

relinquish vs. delegate: To relinquish a duty is stronger than to delegate it: you give it up completely and permanently, keeping no oversight at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away, off (Latin)

Root — leg

Root — leg: to send with a task; to appoint (from Latin legare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb-forming ending: to make or do

Put it together

Put it together: Delegate is literally to send duties away (de-) to a person you appoint (legare) — you dispatch a piece of your workload into someone else's hands while remaining the one in charge.

Use the root in a new word: relegate

Use the root in a new word: relegate: After the losing season, the team was relegated — sent down — to a lower division.

Root Check

Word Choice

Workplace / leadership

This card teaches delegate as a verb: good leaders delegate tasks they don't need to do personally. English also has a noun delegate — a person sent to represent others at a national conference — pronounced with a softer ending (/DEL-uh-git/). Keep the verb firmly in the world of handing off work and responsibility; it is not a word about settling arguments or disputes.
